newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Mandela gives Tiny Rowland SAfrica's highest award.
newsitem.headline: Mandela gives Tiny Rowland SAfrica's highest award.

text.p: President Nelson Mandela awarded South Africa's highest award to controversial British businessman "Tiny" Rowland on Wednesday for his contribution to peace and prosperity in Africa.

Rowland, who built the obscure African colonial company Lonhro into a vast empire to become one of Britain's most successful businessmen, was awarded the Order of Good Hope Class III as "an expression of the gratitude and esteem of the government and people of South Africa".

The citation to the award said Rowland had always been sensitive to the political and social interests of the country and had made an invaluable contribution to bringing peace and prosperity to African countries.
"He unselfishly used his good offices in many situations as a mediator between parties in conflict," it read.
Rowland was also honoured for his generosity to activists in exile, particularly African National Congress chairman Oliver Tambo, whom he supported financially until he died in 1993.
Mandela handed the award to Rowland at his presidential mansion in Pretoria in the presence of Tambo's son, Dali, and other family members.
The tycoon's pugnacious style has earned him enemies and even the company he established threw him out in 1995, alleging "public and irreconcilable differences".
Britain's political and financial establishment was often jarred by Rowland's style, which former Conservative Prime Minister Edward Heath once called the "unacceptable face of capitalism".
